title: Nike joins F1 as apparel partner
article_text:
Athletic apparel giant Nike has joined F1 as its official partner and uniform supplier, taking over from Puma at the start of 2027.

As was long rumoured, Nike will start supplying F1 personnel with apparel and footwear form the start of next season, a partnership that also extends to F1 Academy, which had both been using Puma kit until this year.

The athletic company will also come up with F1-inspired retail collections, the first of which will go on sale on Friday and be centred around the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

"Nike will bring new energy to the pinnacle of motorsport through capsule collections with a focus on style, performance, and lifestyle including footwear, apparel, and accessories, as well as performance innovations, and race-weekend experiences for the next generation of athletes and fans," the announcement promised.

"Fans will get a first look on 20 November, when the limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection drops at the F1 Hub and Nike Las Vegas stores.

Nike CEO Elliott Hill said: "Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate. That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world.”

title: Formula 1 and Nike join forces in long-term partnership
article_text:
From 2027, Nike will become an Official Partner of Formula 1 and the sport’s Official Apparel and Uniform Supplier, bringing together two of the world’s most influential brands at the intersection of sport, speed and culture.

Formula 1 have announced a long-term partnership with Nike, bringing together two of the world’s most influential brands at the intersection of sport, speed, and culture.

United by a relentless drive to push boundaries, Nike will bring new energy to the pinnacle of motorsport through capsule collections with a focus on style, performance, and lifestyle including footwear, apparel, and accessories, as well as performance innovations, and race-weekend experiences for the next generation of athletes and fans.

Beginning in 2027, Nike will join Formula 1 as an Official Partner and become the sport's Official Apparel and Uniform Supplier, creating co-branded uniforms worn by staff across F1 events worldwide.

The partnership will come to life throughout the global race calendar, bringing the distinct attitude of racing to fans through collections designed to live beyond the track. Fans will get a first look on 20 November, when the limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection drops at the F1 Hub and Nike Las Vegas stores, ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Formula 1 will also welcome Nike as Official Partner and Official Sporting Apparel Partner of F1 ACADEMY, reinforcing a shared commitment to working with the sport’s next generation of athletes, to develop what they need to perform at their best through Nike’s innovation, design and technology.

As Formula 1 continues to attract new audiences around the world, the partnership will continue to grow, delivering exclusive products, new experiences, and activations designed to bring fans closer to the sport than ever before.

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, said: “Formula 1 and Nike are two of the world’s most iconic brands, united by a relentless drive to innovate, perform at the highest level, and inspire people to push beyond what is possible.

"Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth, reaching hundreds of millions of fans and engaging one of the most passionate, diverse and dynamic communities in sport. Nike’s unique ability to sit at the intersection of sport, culture and inspiration makes them the ideal partner as we enter our next chapter.

“This partnership is a powerful reflection of Formula 1’s scale, ambition and global momentum. Together, we have an extraordinary opportunity to redefine how fans connect with our sport, create lasting impact across both Formula 1 and F1 ACADEMY and inspire the next generation of racers, creators and innovators around the world.

"This is far more than a commercial partnership; it is the coming together of two brands that shape culture, challenge convention and set new standards of excellence. We are only at the start of what we can achieve together, and the possibilities ahead are truly limitless.”

Elliott Hill, President and CEO of Nike, added: “Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate. That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world.”

title: F1 and Whoop in deal aimed at unveiling physical realities of racing
article_text:
Motor racing's top-tier Formula 1 (F1) has struck a multi-year commercial deal with US-based wearable fitness tech brand Whoop.

The deal, signed days before the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 21, sees Whoop become an official partner of F1, with the tie-up revolving around developing "new broadcast storytelling experiences," using collaboration with the drivers to give fans a wider insight into the "physical realities of racing."

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The Las Vegas event has now become one at which brands routinely choose to activate for the first time.

Whoop will now receive trackside branding opportunities at F1 races throughout the length of the partnership, while the tie-up will also be activated across the series' digital, social media, and event-focused platforms.

In addition, Whoop is set to become a sponsor of the F1 Academy female-only subsidiary series. That element of the overall agreement will entail Whoop and F1 Academy working to "showcase the performance, dedication, and potential of the next generation of female racing drivers."

Stefano Domenicali, Formula 1's president and chief executive (CEO), has commented: "This partnership with Whoop opens up an incredibly exciting new chapter for our sport. For the first time we’ll be able to bring fans even closer to understanding what some of our drivers experience physically and mentally during the most intense moments of a race."

Commercially speaking, last week, F1 announced aerospace innovation brand Archer as a new partner, in a deal aimed at bringing a new element to the VIP fan experience at its Grands Prix.

Archer becomes an official supporter of F1, a new sponsorship tier created through this partnership.

The tie-up will involve both parties looking at ways to introduce an all-electric air-taxi service – featuring vertical take-off and landing features – at select F1 events in the future.

Up to this point, F1 had four tiers of sponsorship – global partners, official partners, regional partners, and official suppliers.

Will Ahmed, founder and CEO of Whoop, added: "Now, for the first time, we can show what happens inside a driver's body during the most intense moments of a race. This will change how fans experience Formula 1 and ultimately deepen our understanding of human performance.“

Earlier this year, Whoop was valued at just over $10 billion after a funding round that included high-profile investment companies and athletes such as Cristiano Ronaldo and LeBron James.

The company raised $575 million in Series G funding at a $10.1 billion valuation, with the round led by venture capital firm Collaborative Fund.

Then, at the end of last month, James was unveiled as a Whoop brand ambassador.

Following the Las Vegas Grand Prix, F1 will head to Qatar and then Abu Dhabi for the final two races of 2026; earlier this month, it was confirmed that Italy's Imola track will not be required to step in for either of those venues.

title: F1 bosses close to V8 engines deal from 2030
article_text:
Formula 1 bosses are close to a deal that will see V8 turbo hybrid engines replace the current controversial engines in 2030.

McLaren chief executive officer Zak Brown said an "agreement in principle" had been reached by engine manufacturers and F1 bosses on the new rules.

These will be for a 2.1-litre V8 turbo engine with a smaller electrical element than this year, as first revealed by BBC Sport last month.

Some details remain to be resolved but the main core of the rules has been agreed.

The electrical element will be for a maximum power output of 200kW - compared with 350kW this year.

But only half of that will be available at all times, with the remaining half used only for an overtake mode.

A key element of the rules will be to remove the issue of energy starvation that has been criticised by the drivers this year for taking away "pure" racing.

But the overall power output of the engines will be similar to now.

The combustion engine will have about 780bhp, while 200kW is 270bhp.

That means a total power output of 1,050bhp in overtake mode or just over 900bhp in standard running.

Brown said: "Everyone is very, very excited. Now it's about kind of dotting the i's and crossing the t's.

"I'm excited for the new engines, I think everyone will be, the power units. But there's a lot more also going on to continue to evolve the sport. So, between the FIA and Formula 1, they're doing a great job."

Alpine executive director Flavio Briatore said: "We have the agreement, basically. It's not signed, but it looks like everybody's agreed to 2030 V8s, and I'm very happy.

"It's the right way to go. We need an engine with a lot of noise, and a simple engine, and we need to be racing with that."

The ruleset amounts to a compromise reached by manufacturers after FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem initially pushed for a naturally aspirated engine without turbo or electrical components.

But these were required to reduce overall fuel consumption, and therefore weight at the start of races.

That means Ben Sulayem's desire for a return to the loud volumes of the previous V8 era from 2006 to 2013 will not be achieved. The engines are expected to sound similar to now.

This was important because a significant increase in engine noise would have put at threat some races in city centres that are commercially important to F1, such as Miami and Las Vegas.

The 2.1-litre capacity has been arrived at because it amounts to adding to two cylinders to the current 1.6-litre V6 blocks, with the aim of reducing development costs.

Cars are expected to start races with about 110-120kg of fuel, up from about 100kg now. A total weight limit of 150kg for the power-units will be imposed, down by about 30kg from the current engines.

There will be a fuel energy flow limit to keep the power of the combustion engine under control, and a budget cap figure for engines set at $190m (£145m) per year.

As part of negotiations, General Motors, backers of the Cadillac team, will delay the production of its new engine until 2030. It had been scheduled for 2029.

In return, GM will lose its voting rights on current engine rules and be classified as a new manufacturer from 2030.

The team will continue to use Ferrari customer engines through 2029.

Cadillac F1 chief executive officer Dan Towriss said: "For a period of time, we were working on both. So, they've already got a V6 base to build off of, and working towards the V8.

"There are a number of designs that are in motion now, and so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in."

title: MLB’s Local Media Rights Emerge As Focus in Labor Fight
article_text:
The future of MLB’s local media business has become a central element in the sport’s labor battle, providing yet another substantial layer to the already fractious situation.

For the last six months, MLB club owners have proposed to pool the local media revenue of all 30 clubs as part of a sought-after economic system that would implement a hard salary cap and floor. Most recently, management has updated its cap offer to the MLB Players Association to a 2028 implementation, and vows there will be “no compromise” on the pursuit of a cap as the Dec. 1 expiration of the current labor deal and an expected lockout thereafter approach.

The pooling of local media revenues, and a promise to end regional blackouts that have long frustrated fans, were also part of a video recently distributed by MLB to fans.

Throughout the entrenched negotiations, though, two key questions have persisted: Why are the local media and salary cap issues so deeply linked, and why couldn’t owners just agree on their own to pool that revenue, similar to how the NFL operates?

The beginning of the answer lies in the accelerating economic divide between the local media revenue of well-heeled teams such as the Dodgers, Yankees, and Mets, and half the league that has lost traditional regional sports network rights deal entirely and now has its local games produced and distributed by MLB—often at less lucrative terms than what they had before.

That split, exacerbated by existential disruption across the media business, has been the key driver in a $446 million spending difference this year between the Dodgers’ total luxury-tax payroll and projected taxes, and the comparable figure for the Guardians.

The total pool of local media income in MLB has also fallen, with the roughly $2.4 billion in annual revenues earlier this decade now standing at about $1.8 billion. With a cap-based system, MLB believes it can both narrow the economic spread and enlarge the overall pie of local media revenue.

“We are trying to make changes to the game that fans want and will improve the value of our media rights,” MLB EVP of baseball operations Morgan Sword said in a presentation this week to reporters.

One of the teams whose games are produced by the league, the Brewers, won this year’s World Series, something Sword called out of step with the industry’s prevailing trends.

“It is truly aberrational in baseball for small markets to be successful,” he said. “It’s not impossible, but it is much, much more difficult in our sports than it is in any of the other sports.”

The second part of the question is more complicated. Pooling local media revenue has a direct connection to MLB’s revenue-sharing system, which is collectively bargained between the league and MLBPA due to its link to player compensation. In the current labor deal, teams currently pay 48% of their local revenue into a central pool. So the league says it cannot simply restructure this part of its economics without involving the union.

While that is indeed true, the blackouts remain a separate issue from a salary cap. A complete pooling of local media revenue, and an end to regional blackouts, could be negotiated with the union absent a salary cap, though that likely would create disruption in the current rights deals—something the league is reluctant to face.

Instead, management is seeking to achieve the local media pooling with a hard cap that players have long resisted. The league is also proposing several other sweeping changes in conjunction with the cap-and-floor system, including significant restrictions on free agency, a retooled draft, and a 154-game regular season.

“We’re not saying it’s the players’ fault there are blackouts. We’re also not saying a salary cap in isolation fixes blackouts,” Sword said. “What we are saying is that this economic system, which is a big series of trade-offs, for the clubs, for the players, enables us to do it.”

MLB additionally is looking to mimic the NBA’s recent strategy and pursue a much more nationalized strategy when its current rights deals expire after the 2028 season. The NBA did that to great success, nearly tripling its national deals to about $6.9 billion annually.

Amid all of that, the MLBPA has consistently argued that caps reduce overall player compensation, pit player against player in a zero-sum game, and erode contract covenants.

“There can be no clearer example of the league’s lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts,” MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer said in a statement. “There should be no illusions about the owners’ true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.”

title: FIFA Under-17 World Cup 2026 gets under way in Qatar despite USA withdrawal
article_text:
The FIFA Under-17 World Cup has kicked off in Qatar, with 48 teams participating in the global youth football competition despite the United States’ withdrawal over security concerns last week.

The tournament, which opened with two concurrent matches on Thursday, will be played in the 2022 World Cup host nation over the next 24 days after FIFA dismissed security concerns in the country.

“Everyone is safe in Doha,” FIFA President Gianni Infantino said in the Qatari capital last week.

US Soccer withdrew its national team citing safety concerns last Thursday, but the sport’s global governing body, which is hosting the tournament, said at the time that its plans remained unchanged.

Qatar has not been targeted by missiles since July as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran.

“The safety and security of all participants and fans remain paramount. As with all FIFA tournaments and events, we are in close contact with the relevant authorities and are looking forward to the tournament kickoff in Qatar,” FIFA told Al Jazeera in a statement hours after the USA’s announcement.

“In recent months, Qatar has successfully hosted several international events,” it added.

Qatar hosted two major international tournaments in the past two weeks.

MotoGP’s Qatar Grand Prix was successfully held on November 8 and the FIP Padel World Cup 2026 ended on the same day.

The tournament will be hosted at the competition complex in Aspire Zone, Qatar’s central sporting hub.

The December 13 final will be played at the Ahmad bin Ali Stadium, which was a FIFA World Cup 2022 venue.

title: Palmowski makes history as she secures pole in Las Vegas
article_text:
Red Bull Racing's Alisha Palmowski secured pole position for the F1 ACADEMY Las Vegas Feature Race.

Alisha Palmowski delivered in her final F1 ACADEMY Qualifying session, leading from the halfway mark to take her seventh pole position of the season by the largest margin in the series' history.

The Red Bull Racing driver was untouchable through the second half of the 30-minute session, after topping the timesheets during the afternoon wet Practice session. After setting an initial benchmark lap time, Palmowski took a firm grip at the top of the timesheets with a 2m 9.915s effort to set her largest margin in a Qualifying session.

Emma Felbermayr crossed the line in second, cutting Palmowski’s advantage down to 1.578s, with Alba Larsen a further 1.671s behind in third. The Audi driver picked up two three-place grid penalties in the Practice session, dropping her to fifth, promoting Larsen to P2, and moving Megan Bruce into the top three.

Nina Gademan fought hard but had to settle for fifth. The Alpine driver will line up in fourth after Felbermayr’s penalty, with Natalia Granada in sixth.

Ella Lloyd couldn't convert her initial wet-tyre pace onto slicks and will line up seventh, followed by Mathilda Paatz, who will start on pole position for Friday’s Reverse Grid Race.

Jade Jacquet qualified in ninth while Ella Stevens rounded out the top 10.

The series’ Las Vegas weekend will continue with the Reverse Grid Race, which is set to start at 18:15 local time on Saturday with Paatz starting on pole position. Until then, you can read a full report from today’s F1 ACADEMY Qualifying session on the official website.

title: F1 to introduce full-time race stewards from 2027
article_text:
Formula 1's governing body the FIA is to introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season.

The move follows consistent calls from grand prix drivers for the change because of criticisms of inconsistency of decisions regarding penalties for on-track incidents.

The FIA said in a statement that it would begin recruiting permanent stewards, and was planning a "phased introduction" during the 2027 season.

The FIA statement added: "The introduction of dedicated full-time stewards to the FIA's flagship championship will provide continuity and expertise within the stewarding structure, further advancing the FIA's commitment to fairness through the ongoing review and continuous improvement of sporting regulations and stewarding guidelines.

"It will also allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making."

It said that the use of driver stewards, usually an ex-F1 driver, would continue, "recognising the invaluable expertise they bring".

The plan is for "a small number" of full-time stewards to be recruited during 2027 and the group to be expanded from 2028.

"Existing FIA stewards will continue to play a vital role, contributing their experience within a mixed roster of full-time and part-time stewards for the foreseeable future," the statement said.

In reality, the move is not a major step on from the current situation, where a small number of stewards are rotated around races.

Each grand prix has a group of four stewards, one of which is an ex-driver.

Current drivers have often referenced the fact that they had repeatedly complained during briefings with FIA officials that rulings on driver standards and racing errors were not applied on a consistent basis.

Last year, Williams driver Carlos Sainz, a director of drivers' body the Grand Prix Drivers' Association, said: "F1 and the FIA all agree that [permanent stewards] should be the way forward, where at least two of the three stewards are permanent and we have one rotational for teaching purposes."

The decision follows the opening of an FIA race operations centre at F1's Biggin Hill headquarters in south London.

The FIA has in recent years received increased income from F1 - which provides the majority of its funding - on the basis that this would be applied to improving officialdom and rule-making.

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said: "This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula 1 World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport."

title: Cadillac scraps V6 F1 engine, delays entry as PU manufacturer
article_text:
CEO Dan Towriss says Cadillac will remain a Ferrari customer team for another year. General Motors has postponed the introduction of its own F1 power unit until the arrival of the V8 in 2030

Cadillac is set to delay the introduction of its in-house Formula 1 power unit by a year to 2030.

The American squad's initial plan was to compete in the championship with its own General Motors power unit for the first time in 2029. However, that was based on the idea that the current regulations cycle would run its full course and that the next generation of power units would not be introduced until 2031.

That situation has since changed. Ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the teams and manufacturers reached an agreement in principle on bringing forward the return of V8 engines, as the McLaren CEO Zak Brown also publicly confirmed during the team principals' press conference on Thursday.

The signatures have not yet been put on paper, as Alpine team principal Flavio Briatore added, but an agreement has been reached on a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 with a reduced proportion of electrical power from 2030.

This development has implications for General Motors' plans. If the American manufacturer were to press ahead with its intention to turn Cadillac into a works team as early as 2029, GM would have to develop a power unit to the current specifications for just a single season. That would be a costly undertaking.

Asked by Motorsport.com whether it would therefore make more sense to continue as a customer team for an extra season, CEO Dan Towriss confirmed in Las Vegas: "Yes, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through 2029 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8."

Towriss sees the arrival of the V8 as a positive development for the sport, and one that Cadillac supports.

"Yeah, I mean, I think we're glad to see really the series coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030. We're super happy with that," Towriss said.

He added that Cadillac and General Motors are approaching another milestone. In less than a month's time, their dedicated power unit facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, will open.

"Yes, our new power unit facility opens up on December 18th. So as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, having this direction is obviously very helpful. We're excited about the direction and the crew's hard at work getting ready."

Besides being expected to appeal more to fans, the V8 is also intended to be simpler and cheaper, which is likewise good news for a newcomer.

When the facility begins operations, Cadillac will initially still be working on both V6 and V8 designs, although the current generation of power units will no longer need to be fully developed for 2029.

"Well, for a period of time, we're working on both. So they've already got a V6 base to build off of and then we’re working towards the V8," Towriss explained.

"There are a number of designs that are in motion now, so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in."

This should lead to the introduction of Cadillac's first in-house power unit in 2030, officially making the American newcomer a works team. That long-term ambition was also important in securing approval for its F1 entry, as the other teams saw it as the main source of added value for F1 as a whole.

title: TAB Replaces Aquis Australia as Gold Coast Turf Club Naming Rights Partner from November 2026

title: BNW Developments expands sporting footprint as Principal Partner of Arabian Aces
article_text:
BNW Developments, one of the UAE’s leading luxury real estate developers, has revealed that it is a Principal Partner of Arabian Aces at the ongoing Abu Dhabi T10 2026, as it looks to contribute to international cricket, connect better with communities, and build meaningful partnerships based on shared values.

With the tournament underway at Zayed Cricket Stadium, BNW Developments is prominently featured on the front of the franchise’s jersey, marking another significant milestone in the company’s growing association with global sporting platforms.

The partnership brings together two ambitious brands on one of cricket’s most dynamic stages. As Arabian Aces competes in the tournament’s tenth edition, BNW Developments is leveraging the association to connect with cricket enthusiasts across the UAE and international markets.

Ankur Aggarwal, Chairman and Founder, BNW Developments, said, “Cricket has a remarkable ability to bring people together across cultures, communities and generations. Led by captain Moeen Ali, Arabian Aces features a mix of international experience and T10 talent, including Andre Russell, Liam Livingstone and Sam Billings.

Pankaj Jain, Co-owner, Arabian Aces, said, “Having BNW Developments on board as our Principal Partner is an important addition to the Arabian Aces journey. title: ‘I’m part of a family’ – Mercedes’ first female junior Fluxa Cross on her F1 ACADEMY debut and Silver Arrows support
article_text:
Mercedes junior Luna Fluxa Cross reflects on how she is feeling ahead of her F1 ACADEMY debut in Las Vegas.

Luna Fluxa Cross has been one of the most talked about up-and-coming female drivers for the past few years. Now the Mercedes junior is preparing for the biggest stage of her career so far as she makes her F1 ACADEMY debut on the streets of Las Vegas.

Fluxa Cross is competing as the Wild Card entry for Round 6, a one-off appearance created to strengthen the talent pool in the regions where the all-female series races.

Competing in the Spanish F4 Championship this season, the 16-year-old faces a steep learning curve. She needs to adapt to a new car, a new team in Hitech and new tyres alongside racing on a street circuit for the first time. On top of that comes the jet lag that challenges every driver on an overseas round.

“It feels amazing,” she said. “I'm really grateful to be the last Wild Card of the season, especially here in Vegas. It's a very nice track and my first street circuit, so I'm looking forward to getting the weekend started.

“It’s going to be about learning and let's see if we can extract the most out of it. I've done some gym sessions and of course [I have a] jet lag plan to get used to all the times. I have everything all ready, so it's very exciting and I'm very looking forward to getting out on track.”

Mercedes spotted Fluxa Cross’ talent long before this weekend. Back in 2022, aged just 11, she became the first female driver to join the Mercedes-AMG F1 Junior Programme. She is now the longest-standing junior in their roster.

Gwen Lagrue has headed the programme since 2016 — he leaves to become Director of the Red Bull Junior Programme in 2027 — and has scouted many of motorsport's brightest stars, not least Formula 1 World Champion Kimi Antonelli and eight-time Grand Prix winner George Russell.

The Silver Arrows’ faith in the Spaniard has proved well-deserved. Fluxa Cross was chosen as part of the inaugural karting cohort for F1 ACADEMY DISCOVER YOUR DRIVE in the Champions of the Future Academy Program International Series in 2024. Seizing the opportunity, she dominated the season. She became the first female winner of an FIA international championship since 1966 and claimed the OK-N Senior title by 125 points.

Mercedes’ support has continued to strengthen since she moved to single-seaters this season, and Fluxa Cross stressed the pivotal role the team has played in getting her to this milestone moment.

“It's been a very long journey with them which I'm very grateful for,” she noted. “It feels like I’m part of a family. They've helped me a lot not only trackside but also in training and nutrition.

“Also outside of track, [Mercedes are] helping me keeping my head in the right mindset and knowing how to approach every weekend. I think they have a really big role in my journey and my career.”

The Wild Card initiative has become a key component of the series’ driver market and a pathway for the next generation of talent. Since its introduction in 2024, nine Wild Cards have earned a full-time seat the following season, including 2026 Champion Alisha Palmowski. Meanwhile, Payton Westcott earned her spot with Mercedes after an impressive debut in Las Vegas last year.

This season, Chiara Battig set a high bar, becoming the first Wild Card driver to achieve a pole position and a podium in Silverstone. However, the Red Bull Junior has also been the only Wild Card entry to score points in 2026.

Looking to add herself to that list, Fluxa Cross isn’t oblivious to what a successful weekend could mean for her future but is choosing to focus on the challenge in front of her rather than what others think she’s capable of.

Asked if points were her target this weekend, she responded jokingly: “Yeah of course, that’s a silly question (laughs).

“I think it's better to go without expectations and see how the weekend plays out. Of course, I’m a Wild Card, so it's my first round in this series. Getting to learn everything and getting up to terms, it’s going to be more tricky for me, but I'm looking forward the challenge and let's see how it plays out.”

She added: “It's very crucial that I show what I'm capable of as it's a good opportunity for a seat next year.

"Also on the other hand, it's just to enjoy it. I do the sport to enjoy it and because that's where I get the results. I'll just go out there with a clear mind and just drive as I know how to.”

title: Pope Leo XIV names Merckx, Indurain, Seixas, Vollering and up to 100 cyclists at the Vatican
article_text:
The Vatican will host an unusual meeting for professional cycling next Monday, November 23. Pope Leo XIV will receive a hundred representatives of this sport, including legends like Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault, and Miguel Induráin, along with current champions like Demi Vollering and Paul Seixas. An audience that also recalls the previous visits of Peter Sagan and Egan Bernal to Pope Francis, both with very special bicycles as protagonists.

The International Cycling Union (UCI) has officially announced that the meeting will take place on the morning of Monday, November 23, in the Vatican. The initiative is organized together with the Dicastery for Culture and Education of the Holy See and will feature a representation from the main cycling disciplines, including para-cycling.

It will not only be a meeting of riders. Among the approximately 100 guests are also representatives from national federations and organizers of major men's and women's tours, as well as officials from other international competitions.

The list of participants includes some of the most important names in the history of cycling. Among them will be Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault, Miguel Induráin, Greg LeMond, Christopher Froome, Vincenzo Nibali, Mark Cavendish, and Francesco Moser.

One of the most curious details is that Eddy Merckx was already received by Pope Paul VI on May 16, 1974, so he will return to the Vatican more than half a century later to meet another pontiff.

On the other generational end is Paul Seixas. The Frenchman, only 20 years old and becoming one of the great references of new cycling, will be one of the youngest representatives at this audience.

The participation of women will also have a significant weight. Demi Vollering, Annemiek van Vleuten, Jeannie Longo, Elisa Longo Borghini, and Mariana Pajón, double Olympic champion of BMX Racing, are announced.

Among the guests is also Spanish Ricardo Ten, a reference in para-cycling, and Ukrainian Anna Kolyzhuk, who suffered a severe spinal injury during a competition in Italy earlier this year.

The president of the UCI, David Lappartient, explained that the meeting represents "an opportunity to reinforce the sporting commitment of cycling in promoting peace and intercultural dialogue among peoples", according to Vatican News.

At the end of the audience, a ceremony is planned in which the UCI will symbolically deliver several bicycles intended for young people in vulnerable situations assisted by Caritas of Rome.

The relationship between the Vatican and professional cycling is not new. In fact, images of cyclists delivering bicycles to the Pope have already featured in several previous meetings.

In January 2018, Peter Sagan visited Pope Francis and gifted him a personalized Specialized Venge, decorated with the white and yellow colors of the Vatican, the Argentine flag, and the coat of arms of the Holy See. The Slovak also presented him with a dedicated rainbow jersey during a visit accompanied by his family.

That bicycle would eventually have a charitable destination. In June 2020, Francis made it available for the charitable initiative We Run Together, which raised funds to support healthcare personnel from two Italian hospitals during the pandemic. Sagan's Specialized was ultimately sold for 30,000 euros.

A few years later, in June 2021, it was Egan Bernal who went to the Vatican after being crowned the winner of the Giro d'Italia. The Colombian brought a maglia rosa and a Pinarello Dogma F12 specially decorated with the colors of Argentina.

For Bernal, that meeting had a significance that went far beyond cycling. In statements collected at the time by Vatican News, he said: "It was the most important experience for me, more important than the Tour de France and the Giro d'Italia."

The story of that bicycle had a second chapter. As we published in March 2024, the Pinarello Dogma F12 that Bernal had given to the Pope appeared in a Catawiki auction.

The bicycle, with exclusive decoration, Shimano Ultegra group, and rim brakes, had a sale estimate that could reach 30,000 euros.

However, the auction ended on March 24, 2024, with a final price of 14,000 euros, after 47 bids. The buyer was a French collector who outbid another Italian bidder.

Now it will be Leo XIV who continues this relationship between cycling and the Holy See. The pontiff already had a first notable contact with the professional peloton in June 2025, when the Giro d'Italia passed through the Vatican in its final stage and received the papal blessing.

title: World Cup halo, Netflix and LA28: Can the NWSL capitalise on its once-in-a-generation opportunity?
article_text:
American sporting exceptionalism has long defined the country’s relationship with men’s soccer.

The world’s most popular sport has traditionally struggled to gain a foothold in a market where American football is king and baseball is woven into the national identity. The 1994 men’s Fifa World Cup catalysed the creation of Major League Soccer (MLS), but the tournament’s legacy was slow-burning, and a men’s national team that never threatened the latter stages of major competition prevented the sport from being thrust into the limelight.

Indeed, many still regarded soccer as a “foreign” pursuit best played by women and children. But it was precisely this attitude that created opportunities for female athletes at college level and on the global stage.

The US women’s national team are one of the dominant forces in the international game, and their victory in the 1999 Fifa Women’s World Cup delivered American soccer’s most iconic moment. The image of Brandi Chastain removing her shirt in celebration adorned the front page of national newspapersy, catapulting the sport into the mainstream.

The triumph renewed calls for greater investment in women’s soccer, setting in motion nearly three decades of growth (with a few hiccups along the way) that have coincided with rising popularity of the sport in general.

MLS is now firmly established, coverage of foreign competitions has gone from the periphery of sports media onto network television, and the 2026 men’s World Cup in North America was a national event in a way that USA 94 was not.

According to Nielsen, the number of people in the US identifying as soccer fans jumped from 66.8 million in July 2025 to 75.2 million in July 2026. Over the past five years, the growth rate has been 26 per cent.

Now, women’s soccer is ready to take up the baton and build on that momentum for sport’s entire ecosystem in the US. Next year’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil kicks off a four-year cycle that includes a new National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) broadcast deal, further expansion, the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games, and the 2031 Women’s World Cup in North America.

“I’ve always wondered when Americans are going to begin to pay attention to this sport of soccer that the rest of the world is enjoying,” NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman told the Leaders Week sports business conference in London.

“But the [appreciation for the] culture around the game, the respect for the game [and] the appreciation for the unique attributes of the game that we had in America around the World Cup gave me a lot of enthusiasm and excitement about the future.”

Along with the Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA), the NWSL is the most high-profile professional women’s team competition in the US. Now in its 14th season, the league’s business is booming by almost every measure. Match attendances, TV viewership and franchise valuations have all climbed considerably in recent years amid growing fan and investor interest.

Commercial rights values have never been higher, while a historic collective bargaining agreement (CBA), agreed in 2024 and running until 2030, delivered better pay and working conditions for players.

Average attendances rose by ten per cent during the first half of the 2026 campaign, while a game between Denver Summit and the Washington Spirit drew 63,004 fans to Empower Field at Mile High, a record for both the league and US women’s professional sport. Earlier this month, Gotham FC raised US$100 million at a record US$350 million valuation, and the league itself hopes to expand to 32 teams in the future.

These metrics are crucial as the league and its partner IMG take the NWSL’s domestic broadcast rights to market. Next season is the last to be covered by four-year US$240 million pacts with CBS, ESPN, Amazon Prime Video and Scripps’ Ion.

The NWSL’s current media strategy is designed to cast the net as wide as possible at the expense of consolidation. CBS offers network coverage and a committed audience of soccer fans on Paramount+, ESPN is the most important sports platform in the country, Amazon Prime reaches streaming-first and younger viewers, and Ion has a growing portfolio of women’s sports rights.

Broadcast ratings for the 2026 regular season were a mixed bag. Viewership on ESPN was static and down ten per cent on CBS, while Roku stepped in as a fifth partner after the collapse of Victory+. But the deals have been successful from a revenue, discoverability and audience expansion perspective.

Berman will be confident that the league’s growing audience, broadcaster demand for live sport and the fees commanded by the WNBA will lead to another improved deal – not to mention rising interest in soccer following the World Cup. And, if nothing else, the addition of two new teams in 2028, when the new deals begin, will increase inventory.

“The next 12 months are going to be critically important and foundational for the next stage of growth for the NWSL,” Berman said. “Our biggest growth opportunity is continuing to build and scale audience.

“Our media deal had us really lean into the discoverability of our property. So, we have incredible partners in ESPN, CBS, Amazon and Ion [and Roku]. Our audience is really spread across multiple channels and so we’re really working hard to prioritise key matches and aggregate audience, so that we can really go into this next cycle continuing to build on the strength of the NWSL.”

The league is tight-lipped about whether it will continue with five partners. ESPN’s coverage of the final round of regular season matches, which saw it broadcast all eight games in a single window, showed the benefits of consolidation. The Disney-owned broadcaster has also scheduled some matches in primetime to fill the gap left by MLB, giving the league further reach and prominence.

title: NBA adds Novig as prediction market partner; AEG joins wave with OG.com
article_text:
US basketball’s elite NBA has followed up its recent deals with Polymarket and Kalshi by adding another prediction market operator to its portfolio through a deal with Novig.

The agreement makes Novig the league’s fourth authorized prediction market partner, The Athletic has reported.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As part of the tie-up, Novig will abide by what the NBA has described as “enhanced integrity obligations specific to prediction markets.”

The league partnered with prominent prediction market operators Polymarket and Kalshi in late October.

The NBA also expanded its partnership with fantasy sports and gaming operator DraftKings, one of its official sportsbook partners, to include prediction markets.

The agreements with Polymarket and Kalshi give the companies the right to leverage NBA data, statistics, and, perhaps crucially, NBA intellectual property (including logos and imagery) in their operations as the league’s ‘preferred prediction-market exchanges’.

In return, the league will be able to govern what NBA-related markets the pair can and cannot offer, as well as prohibit trading on NBA events by all league and team personnel, with the NBA also to collaborate with Polymarket and Kalshi for information sharing around any investigations regarding illicit and suspicious trading.

To facilitate those agreements, the NBA struck a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the regulatory body that oversees the prediction market industry) to ensure proper oversight of the prediction market business.

The NBA has followed the lead of the National Hockey League, Major League Soccer, UFC, and Major League Baseball, all of which struck agreements with Polymarket and/or Kalshi in the past year.

The NBA is, perhaps, the most prominent among all of these sports properties, and second in the US only to the NFL in terms of reach.

The NFL remains the last major men’s sports property in the US without a Polymarket or Kalshi partnership, and that may remain the case for the foreseeable future, according to comments NFL commissioner Roger Goodell made last month.

Goodell recently said that the NFL would not partner with either until there are stronger federal guardrails.

Earlier this year, Novig partnered with LIV Golf, the beleaguered international golf tour that is reportedly set to wind down its operations.

Meanwhile, Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG), the California-based sports and entertainment company, has entered the prediction market business through a multi-property partnership with OG.com.

The tie-up makes OG.com, the prediction market and trading platform launched by Crypto.com, the exclusive prediction market platform partner for AEG’s Los Angeles sports and entertainment properties, including Crypto.com Arena, the LA Kings NHL franchise, and the LA Live entertainment district.

The partnership will combine prominent branding, digital integrations, and exclusive fan rewards.

At Crypto.com Arena, the partnership will include in-arena visibility and opportunities for OG.com to engage guests through targeted promotions, while at LA Live, the brand will be featured across the district’s digital signage network.

In addition, OG.com and the LA Kings will also introduce a series of interactive fan experiences, exclusive rewards, and special events throughout the NHL season, including OG.com being the presenting partner of an upcoming game in March at Crypto.com Arena.

The brand will also benefit from in-game visibility during LA Kings home games, including digitally enhanced and static dasherboard signage, as well as integration into social media content.

title: "Same as Brazil" – Red Bull "trying to understand" the root cause of Max Verstappen's complaints
article_text:
Pierre Waché clarifies after the opening practice sessions that Red Bull is dealing with a balance issue again. The team has not yet been able to test its minor upgrade in Las Vegas due to the rain

After Thursday's practice sessions in Las Vegas, Red Bull – like all Formula 1 teams – has been left with very few answers. Isack Hadjar eventually finished fourth on the timesheets, but that means very little given that no more rain is forecast for the remainder of the weekend.

The conditions were therefore not representative during the practice day, and that was precisely why Max Verstappen stayed in the garage for so long. It was only in the final five minutes, following the late red flag, that the Dutchman set his first timed lap. There was simply very little to learn.

Nevertheless, Verstappen was not happy with the RB22 during his brief appearance on track.

It started with a suspected power unit issue, with Verstappen reporting a lack of power on his out-lap. Red Bull responded by explaining that it was mainly related to the low temperatures and would improve on its own, although Verstappen replied: "This is not normal!"

After the session, technical director Pierre Waché explained the background to these complaints, which were also heard from Verstappen's team-mate Hadjar.

"I think it's mainly energy management and the MGU-K deployment around the lap. There was a little bit of fine-tuning on that aspect to make sure that it's optimised for the lap," Waché said.

"When the grip is so low in these conditions, the adaptation of the energy management takes some time on our side."

However, that was not Verstappen's only complaint. The four-time world champion also said over the team radio: "This car is not good guys, same problem as Brazil."

Waché stressed that this was not related to the DM01 power unit, nor to engine braking – another aspect that has frequently troubled Verstappen this year – but purely to the car's balance.

"No, that's not about the power unit. It’s about the car balance, he was not happy with how the car behaved. We are trying to understand where it's coming from."

In Sao Paulo, Verstappen said that the balance had changed completely after the first stint on intermediates. According to him, this could not be fully explained by the switch to slick tyres, as the car also felt very different during the final laps on inters compared to the opening phase.

During practice in Las Vegas, Verstappen experienced the same balance problems at the rear of the car, something Red Bull will look into ahead of qualifying.

Nevertheless, Hadjar said he has "a good feeling" about this street circuit, although Waché is not yet prepared to fully share that optimism.

"I'm never optimistic. We have a lot of work to do, but it's unknown where we are. I think everybody is bringing some kind of update. Some teams are even bringing some engine updates.

"We will see where we are. It's difficult to say. At the moment, Max is not very happy with the car, and Isack is. We have to work on it and see how we can extrapolate it to tomorrow’s conditions."

While Waché mentioned upgrades, Red Bull has also brought a minor update to the Nevada desert. It involves a small modification to the front wing endplate, which Hadjar has said is worth "less than a tenth".

However, due to the tricky conditions, Red Bull has not yet been able to test the new part and will have to wait until the third practice session to do so.

"Yeah, we also brought some update, we mainly want to test it here. It was planned to test it in FP1, which we were not able to do, and the same for FP2. We have to run it in the dry and we will hope to be able to do it tomorrow morning."

Celsius Is Turning Sports Sponsorships Into a Year-Round Brand Platform
article_text:
Celsius is building a sports marketing system rather than betting on one big sponsorship. The energy drink brand is combining college football, Formula 1, running communities and fitness competitions to make its better-for-you positioning visible wherever active consumers already gather.

Celsius became the official energy drink sponsor of ESPN’s College GameDay in August, with campus run clubs, tailgates and a multi-year partnership. The brand also used college football NIL deals with analyst Kirk Herbstreit, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore.

The important move is not the size of any individual deal. It is the way Celsius is connecting different sports environments to the same consumer promise.

At the New York City Marathon, the brand returned with a Club Celsius pop-up and a multi-day Brooklyn takeover. It also sponsored Diplo’s Run Club stops in New York, Chicago and Los Angeles. Earlier in the year, Celsius became the official global energy drink partner of the ATHX Games, a fitness competition.

That gives Live. Fit. Go., the 360-degree campaign launched in 2025 across television, paid and organic social, out-of-home and experiential marketing, more places to show up. A runner, college football fan and Formula 1 viewer may not share a sport, but they can still recognize the same brand behavior: Celsius is present around performance, movement and the rituals that surround them.

Celsius is also extending the strategy into premium global sports. The company signed British driver Jessica Hawkins ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix and continues its multi-year partnership with Aston Martin Aramco in Formula 1.

That range is deliberate. Celsius CMO Kyle Watson told Modern Retail that the brand is not defined by a single sport and wants to build connections across the sports landscape. The approach gives Celsius more chances to meet consumers in context, rather than asking one event or athlete to carry the entire brand story.

There is a practical lesson here for marketers. Sports sponsorship works harder when it creates repeatable participation around the rights deal: a run club, a campus activation, a fan event or a product ritual. The logo may create awareness, but the surrounding behavior gives the partnership a reason to be remembered.

Celsius is effectively using sports as a year-round distribution network for its positioning. The strategic consequence is that future growth will depend less on adding famous names and more on making each new partnership feel like another credible expression of the same active lifestyle.

title: How regulated sponsorship shapes boxing’s commercial model
article_text:
Matchroom Sport Limited, whose group promotes boxing alongside darts, snooker and nine-ball pool, filed its group accounts for the year to 30 June 2025 at Companies House on 12 April 2026. Group turnover was £225.5m, up from £218.3m, and profit for the year was £41.9m. The strategic report credits the boxing companies, Matchroom Boxing Limited and its subsidiaries, with a combined profit of £9.9m, against £11.4m in 2024.

Turnover by destination shifted sharply. The United Kingdom accounted for £115.3m (2024: £87.4m), the rest of Europe for £35.3m and the rest of the world for £74.9m, down from £96.6m. Cost of sales was £144.3m, leaving gross profit of £81.2m. The group averaged 142 employees, with staff costs of £13.9m (2024: £12.7m).

Note 2.4 sets out when each kind of income is booked. Event income and gate receipts are recognised on the date of the event, and broadcasting income on delivery of the live event or the contracted content. Sponsorship income is allocated over the period of the agreement or in line with the size and nature of the events it comes from. The note gives no amount for any category, so the filing cannot show how much of the £225.5m came from sponsors, or whether any came from betting or online casino companies.

Under principal risks and uncertainties, the directors state that any change to gambling legislation may affect the ability of companies in the “Betting and Gaming sector” to use their brands at group events. The strategic report also lists broadcasters, sponsors and the general public as the group’s customers. The accounts name no company and give no figure for the exposure. They treat betting and gaming as one sector and do not separate sportsbooks from an online casino or any other licensed product.

Section Nine of the Ofcom Broadcasting Code, shown as last updated on 5 January 2026, governs sponsorship of television programming. It defines a sponsor as any undertaking or individual, other than a broadcaster or programme producer, funding programming with a view to promoting its products, services, trade marks or activities, and sponsored programming as programming that has had some or all of its costs met by a sponsor. Rule 9.18 bars a sponsor from influencing content or scheduling in a way that impairs the broadcaster’s editorial independence. Rule 9.17 requires sponsorship to comply with the content and scheduling rules that apply to television advertising, and rule 9.16 bars sponsorship by anyone prohibited from advertising on television. Rule 9.19 requires credits to identify the sponsor by name or trade mark and to show its link with the content. Under rule 9.22(b), a credit shown during a programme must be a brief, neutral statement with a static graphic and no advertising messages or calls to action.

Rule 9.13(c) lists “gambling” among the products whose placement in programmes is prohibited. The Code uses that single word, with no separate mention of an online casino or of any other licensed product.

Rule 9.23 adds that where a sponsor is prohibited from product placing in the programme it is sponsoring, its credits may not be shown during that programme, while rule 9.20 still allows credits at the beginning and end.

title: Ondas Partners with Aston Martin F1 Team in Multi-Year Technology Collaboration
article_text:
Ondas Inc. (Nasdaq: ONDS), a developer of autonomous systems and mission-critical technologies, has announced a multi-year partnership with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, becoming a Global Partner of the British racing organization.

The Ondas Aston Martin Formula One partnership will focus on engineering collaboration, technology exchange and data-driven decision-making under a shared initiative called “Speed to Decision.”

The agreement also provides Ondas with a global marketing platform to engage customers, investors and business partners, beginning with branding on Aston Martin’s Formula One car at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The collaboration brings together two organizations operating in different industries but facing similar engineering challenges involving reliability, complex data and time-sensitive decisions.

Ondas develops autonomous systems, robotics and integrated sensing technologies for defense, homeland security, public safety and industrial applications.

Aston Martin Aramco competes in Formula One, where teams continuously analyze vehicle performance, environmental conditions and operational information to make decisions during races.

The partnership is intended to explore how engineering practices developed in these environments can inform technology development and operational execution.

“This partnership brings together two organizations grounded in engineering excellence, rapid innovation and high-performance execution,” said Eric Brock, Chairman and CEO of Ondas.

Brock said the agreement provides opportunities for technical collaboration while expanding Ondas’ engagement with customers, partners and investors.

Beginning in 2027, the partnership will include an annual Engineering Leadership workshop at Aston Martin’s AMR Technology Campus in Silverstone, England.

The workshops will bring together engineering and technology teams from both organizations to examine approaches to rapid development, iterative testing and decision-making.

The companies intend to identify practices that could produce measurable benefits within their respective operations.

However, the announcement does not identify specific joint products, research programs or technology transfers resulting from the agreement.

The partnership’s central theme, “Speed to Decision,” reflects the importance of converting complex information into timely operational decisions.

For Ondas, that concept relates to autonomous platforms and mission-critical technologies operating in demanding environments.

In Formula One, engineering teams must interpret vehicle telemetry, track conditions and strategic information while making decisions under significant time pressure.

Ryan Hartman, President and CEO of Ondas Sentinel, highlighted the similarities.

“Formula One demonstrates what happens when engineering, information and human judgment operate as one system,” Hartman said.

He described the partnership as an opportunity to exchange ideas about using advanced technology to support precise decisions at operational speed.

While the organizations see potential value in sharing engineering practices, the agreement does not announce the integration of Ondas drone technology into Aston Martin’s racing operations.

The partnership will make its public debut during the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Ondas branding will appear on the nose of Aston Martin’s Formula One car, with additional branding on driver race suits beginning in the 2027 season.

The agreement also includes digital content, hospitality experiences and opportunities for engagement with customers and business partners.

Jefferson Slack, Managing Director of Commercial and Marketing at Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, welcomed Ondas as a Global Partner.

“Formula One provides a unique platform for bringing businesses together, building relationships and creating new opportunities,” Slack said.

He highlighted the team’s trackside hospitality and knowledge-sharing opportunities as elements of the relationship.

The financial terms of the partnership were not disclosed.

Ondas provides autonomous and unmanned systems for government, defense and commercial customers.

The company develops technologies intended to support operations where reliable information, automation and rapid decision-making are important.

The Aston Martin partnership is primarily an engineering collaboration and commercial engagement agreement rather than an announced drone development or defense procurement program.

F1 2027 driver lineups: Who has a seat - and who's out of contract?
article_text:
The 2026 rule changes threw Formula 1 into a new era of challenges and uncertainty, but the real moments of unpredictability are still to come.

Most drivers secured short-term deals to survive the regulation shift, leaving the grid wide open for the following year. With only a handful of drivers locked into long-term contracts almost every seat on the grid is up for grabs.

Here is our early look at what the future holds for the current Formula 1 lineup.

Prior to the start of the 2024 F1 season Norris agreed to an "extended multi-year contract beyond 2025."

The reigning champion has now signed a new contract with McLaren until at least 2030. The deal, which includes one of his title-winning Formula 1 cars as a gift from the team, also has the option of a "multi-year" extension beyond 2030.

Ahead of the first race of the 2025 F1 season Piastri also signed a multi-year contract extension. His previous deal already ran until the end of 2026, and his latest agreement is likely to keep him at McLaren until at least the end of 2028 -- though speculation continues to rumble on about his long-term future.

While an exact end date of Hamilton's contract -- signed after completing one of the biggest driver moves in F1 history -- was never officially communicated, Hamilton admitted earlier this year that he still had a contract in place for 2027. That means he got at least a three-year deal at Ferrari, something he had also been seeking at Mercedes.

Amid retirement rumours, Hamilton has also crushed speculation and assured fans that he wasn't going anywhere just yet.

He said: "There's a lot of people that are trying to retire me, and that's not even in my thoughts. I'm already thinking of what will be next, and planning for, like, the next five years. But I still plan to be here for some time."

Leclerc, who first joined Ferrari in 2019, signed another multi-year extension ahead of the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix.

The team did not publicly reveal an exact expiry date, but the new agreement is understood to take Leclerc to 2028 and potentially beyond, giving Ferrari long-term security over one side of its driver lineup.

Red Bull confirmed in 2022 that four-time world champion Verstappen would remain with the team until the end of 2028 in one of the longest deals on the F1 grid.

Sources told ESPN that performance-related clauses in Verstappen's contract could allow him to leave early, but the Dutchman has now signed a new contract extension with Red Bull until 2030 ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix.

Isack Hadjar was promoted from Racing Bulls to partner Verstappen for the 2026 season after an impressive rookie campaign. He has now signed a contract extension with Red Bull, securing his seat for the 2027 season.

Russell agreed a new deal with Mercedes ahead of the 2026 season following lengthy negotiations with team principal Toto Wolff.

Although the agreement was initially confirmed as taking him through at least 2026, Russell has since described it as a multi-year deal and said he will fulfill the performance clauses in his contract to stay at Mercedes next year.

Mercedes' Antonelli has only been given one-year contracts since his debut, but given his form this season there's no way he'll be leaving the Silver Arrows. Right?

No official announcements have been made yet, but Antonelli could be celebrating both a maiden title and a bumper new deal this year.

Alonso's current Aston Martin deal ran until the end of the 2026 season, but the 45-year-old has now confirmed his decision to keep racing with the team through 2027.

Stroll signed a contract extension in 2024 which kept him with Aston Martin for 2025 "and beyond," but no specific end date was announced. Part of that ambiguity, of course, is because he's the son of team owner Lawrence Stroll.

He remains with the team for 2026 and will continue to partner alongside Alonso for 2027.

Gasly is one of the drivers whose future is already settled -- the Frenchman signed a new multi-year agreement with Alpine in 2025 which keeps him locked in at the team until at least the end of the 2028 season.

Colapinto retained his Alpine seat alongside Gasly for 2026 after taking over from Jack Doohan during the previous season. He has now signed a new contract with the team, meaning the Argentinian will continue with Alpine for the 2027 season.

F2 star Câmara will replace Esteban Ocon for the 2027 season on a multi-year agreement. The reigning Formula 3 champion and current Formula 2 leader will make his debut in F1 and will partner fellow Ferrari Driver Academy member Oliver Bearman.

Bearman joined Haas on a multi-year deal when he became a full-time F1 driver in 2025. The exact duration of Bearman's contract has not been made public, leaving his 2027 status uncertain for now.

However, sources with good knowledge of the team's thinking have told ESPN that Bearman is almost certain to stay with the team in 2027 unless a Ferrari seat opens up, then the Englishman remains effectively loaned to Haas.

Lawson remained with Racing Bulls for 2026 after rebuilding his season following a short-lived promotion to Red Bull the previous year.

His seat was only confirmed for the current season, but the New Zealander has proved his case after a series of strong performances, meaning he has now secured his seat for the 2027 season.

title: Charles Leclerc on journalist ban: “I was surprised by the choice of words”
article_text:
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.

Charles Leclerc had no hand in getting a veteran Formula 1 reporter barred from the paddock, and he isn't interested in policing the press - even when the headlines get a little personal.

Addressing the media ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the Ferrari driver spoke for the first time about the FIA’s decision to revoke Daily Mail journalist Jonathan McEvoy’s accreditation for the remaining three rounds of the season.

"I saw the article; I was quite surprised by the choice of words, but apart from that I don’t have much to say," Leclerc said. "Then on the sanction itself, obviously I’ve got absolutely nothing to do with it, and I don’t have much to say about it."

Despite his surprise at the column, Leclerc drew a line between routine media scrutiny and the specific phrasing McEvoy used.

"The only thing I’ll say is that as Formula 1 drivers, I think we are used to this kind of criticism. Not this kind of criticism, but to criticism in general and to critics," Leclerc clarified. "It’s definitely the job of journalists to kind of ask the bad questions and do some of the tough headlines sometimes. But I was surprised with the choice of words."

The controversy began after McEvoy published an opinion piece reflecting on the opening-lap contact between Leclerc and Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the Mexico City Grand Prix, in which he referred to Leclerc as a "sneaky little b*****d".

FIA general manager Alberto Villarreal subsequently notified McEvoy that his accreditation was suspended for Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi, though he is expected to return for the 2027 season. Confirming the sanction, an FIA spokesperson cited the 2026 Formula 1 world championship guidelines, stating that media passes are issued at the governing body's sole discretion and require "the highest standards of fairness and professionalism".

title: Rafael Camara torn between his F2 title bid and more F1 races with Haas
article_text:
Rafael Camara is torn between completing his title-contending Formula 2 campaign and seeing out the 2026 season at Haas in Formula 1.

The Ferrari protege is the reigning F3 champion and leads the F2 standings as a rookie with Invicta Racing, courtesy of a starring campaign in which he has taken five pole positions and seven feature race podiums including three victories.

Esteban Ocon’s fallout with Haas has provided Camara with an opportunity to make his F1 debut at the Brazilian Grand Prix, and he will gain more experience this weekend in Las Vegas ahead of his full rookie campaign with the team in 2027.

However, the last two rounds of the F2 season are taking place alongside F1 in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, so Camara, Haas and Ferrari now have a tough call to make – with the youngster indicating “a mix of people” will be involved in the decision-making.

Asked about the situation, the 21-year-old replied: “Well, that's a very good question. Both of them will be very important for me. In F2, I feel like the whole year you're working for that and for sure you want to finish in a high. And also, I wouldn't be in this position or having the opportunities if it didn't happen, what happened this year in F2 with Invicta. So, for sure, it would be very special.

“At the end of the day, I'll be doing what I love to do, and I'll be happy in doing [either] of them. But it will definitely be a difficult decision to do on my side, because one side, you have Formula 1, something you've always been dreaming of being and doing in your life; and the other side, you have the whole championship and you're working the whole year to close that.

“Let's see. I'll try now to focus on this weekend and finish in a good way. And then hopefully we can sort it out, what will happen after that.”

Interestingly, FIA regulations mean no driver can compete in both F1 and F2 on the same weekend; if Camara does race in the feeder series, Haas can resort to reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa, who made an unexpected grand prix debut in Mexico after Ocon was suddenly dismissed.

Though he currently leads the F2 standings, the Invicta racer is just seven points ahead of Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov, who has missed out on a 2027 F1 graduation with Racing Bulls. Alpine academy members Alex Dunne and Gabriele Mini are respectively 18 and 44 points adrift.

Asked by Motorsport.com how valuable the F2 title would be to his CV and career, Camara commented: “Yeah, I think that would be nice, finishing the F2 season. And for sure, when you [look back on] what you achieved on the junior categories, I think it's something very nice, having the F3 and F2 championship, winning as a rookie. Not only that, but the feeling of winning and doing things will be very nice.

“But I still don't know what will happen and I don't know how I will do it. Like I said, I'm just trying to finish this weekend and then for sure there will be a lot of things to discuss after.”

Haas’ new driver is feeling much more confident ahead of his second grand prix, having gained key experience in tricky wet conditions on his way to a lowly 20th at Interlagos.

“The main takeaways were working with the team and also with how the car behaves,” Camara said of his maiden outing as a race driver. “I think it makes you already starting this weekend much calmer, because in a way you know what to expect.

“It helps starting the weekend with less things in your head, so you can, in a way, focus more into details, more in other things. Probably in Brazil, you're just trying to learn everything at the same time and your brain starts to overheat a bit. For sure it helps.”

title: Zak Brown explains why McLaren keeps selling F1 cars before they race ahead of 2027 auction
article_text:
For McLaren fans. Papaya news from Woking, with the latest on the drivers, the car, team strategy and every race weekend.

McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown has explained why the Woking outfit is selling its Formula 1 cars at auction before they have even turned a wheel, saying the alternative is leaving them hidden away.

McLaren will auction its 2027 car, the MCL41, with RM Sotheby's in Abu Dhabi on 9 December, three days after the season finale. A chassis used by either Lando Norris or Oscar Piastri will be offered with a 2027-specification Mercedes power unit.

It follows last year's sale of this season's car, the MCL40A, which went for a staggering $11.48million at RM Sotheby's Abu Dhabi sale last December. It was the first time an F1 car had been sold before it had raced.

The buyer will not receive that car until 2028, because of rules designed to stop rivals getting access to a team's intellectual property, and was offered a 2025 show car to display in the meantime.

Asked in the team principals' press conference in Las Vegas about the thinking behind the sales, Brown said it made more sense than locking the cars away.

"Yeah, the other alternative is you leave them all on shelves under wraps, which is a shame. We have a great automotive business, we have a very passionate fan base, and we have a certain part of our fan base that has a passion to collect cars," Brown said.

Brown, a keen car collector himself, said last year's buyer had been able to follow their car all season.

"And so last year with Sotheby's, we sold '26 cars and someone had the ability to come on the journey, watch their car race, win some races. And so we're going to do that once a year at least. That's our intention," he said.

McLaren's 2026 car has won three races this season, all with Norris, in Hungary, the Netherlands and Brazil. The team currently sits fourth in the constructors' championship with 398 points, 17 points behind Red Bull in third.

This year's winning bidder will get a tour of McLaren's Woking headquarters before the 2027 season, the chance to meet Brown, Norris and Piastri, and an invitation to the team's 2027 launch.

Brown said the sales gave a small group of fans an experience that would otherwise not exist.

"We have a nice business. We've done 35 track cars of our Le Mans car, so for us it's about experiential opportunities for those fans of ours that are in a privileged position to be able to own Formula 1 cars. Otherwise, we make four or five cars a year and they end up stacking up on a shelf, and that's no good for anybody," he said.

Hot Wheels ‘Tiniest Team Principal’ search opens
article_text:
A global competition to identify three young F1 fans for an official Hot Wheels role and VIP access to a Grand Prix is underway.

Mattel has announced a global search for the first-ever Hot Wheels ‘Tiniest Team Principal’, with one winner to be selected from each of the United States, the United Kingdom, and Mexico.

The winners will also be flown, with their families, to Hot Wheels headquarters in El Segundo, California, where they will meet the design and executive teams behind Hot Wheels and Formula 1, and take part in picking and designing their own Hot Wheels F1 die-cast car.

Each ‘Tiniest Team Principal’ will step into an official ambassador role for the Hot Wheels brand and receive VIP access to a Formula 1 Grand Prix.

The entry period is open now and will run through June 16. Parents or legal guardians of children aged five to ten can submit an entry video on TikTok or Instagram, with official rules available here. Winners will be announced on June 23

Submissions can include custom trackset builds, race predictions, original designs, or a passionate explanation of how they would run an F1 team.

Entries will be reviewed by a judging panel that includes Formula 1 President and CEO Stefano Domenicali, 2009 FIA Formula One World Drivers’ Champion and F1 Ambassador Jenson Button, Mattel’s General Manager and Head of Vehicles and Building Sets Ted Wu, and Hot Wheels designer Kristina Albrecht.

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, said: “In Formula 1, you must be ready to make the big decisions when it matters most. This is a fantastic way to put our youngest fans right at the heart of the action, giving them a unique chance to go behind the scenes for a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

"I’m really looking forward to seeing this evolution of this partnership and the incredible creativity and passion they bring to running their own team… I think some of our current Team Principals might even need to watch out!”

Jenson Button, 2009 FIA Formula One World Drivers’ Champion, added: “In Formula 1, the difference between winning and losing can come down to one decision. Kids make those kinds of calls every time they play with Hot Wheels. I know the Hot Wheels Tiniest Team Principal will keep the rest of the paddock on their toes.”

Ted Wu, General Manager and Global Head of Vehicles and Building Sets at Mattel said: “The task is simple. We are looking for someone who builds, rebuilds, and takes on every challenge. A kid with strong opinions on what makes a car faster, cooler, and more fun. The Tiniest Team Principal might even take my job for the day… as long as I get it back.”
